note: (P/anticipatory-application) This article's named departure from media-richness theory is Strand F's earliest instance of the cluster plan's debate axis 3, later engaged from Strand A (Witmer & Singer technology-determined; Chow SEM psychologically-determined).

Cognitive presence, though most basic, is explicitly 'not sufficient to sustain a critical community of learners' on its own; requires the broader socio-emotional support of social presence (FAITHFUL-Garrison-Anderson-Archer, p.94).
Authors concede the 'vexing problem' of unit-of-analysis reliability remains unresolved in this article, deferred to Rourke et al. (1999) (FE, p.103-104).

(anticipatory-application) vle-01's F7 'Presence & the WE' finding (F1-PRESENCE 4.3 vs 1.2 per-100, APP vs VID) plausibly instantiates this article's social-presence construct within the VLE's own text data; medium differs (3D app/video vs. text conferencing), construct transfers.

(anticipatory-application) vle-03's exemplar quotes on presence, carry-over, and social watching plausibly instantiate participants 'project[ing] themselves socially and emotionally, as real people' in the VLE's own student text data.

(anticipatory-application) The article's departure from media-richness theory offers Part III a resource for interpreting the VLE's APP/VID presence-indicator gap as context-driven (familiarity, task structure, group assignment) rather than purely medium-driven.

(anticipatory-application) Teaching presence as the binding element integrating cognitive and social presence offers Part III language for why VLE design/facilitation choices, not medium alone, may explain variance in student engagement outcomes.

(P/anticipatory-application) Forward-flag: this later unit's title ('Re-examining Social Presence') signals it is very likely to cite this article's canonical social-presence definition directly; this 1999 article could not cite a 2019 paper, so this edge is this cluster's own forward construction, not a citation Garrison, Anderson & Archer make.

(P/anticipatory-application) Forward-flag: a 2017 meta-analysis of social presence in online learning almost certainly cites the CoI framework as foundational; this article predates it by 18 years and could not cite it.
